p: turned to the contrary: This was by God's great providence, who turns the joy of the wicked into sorrow, and the tears of the godly into gladness.
helped the Jews: Honoured them and befriended them.
enemies with the stroke of the: Who had conspired their death by the permission of the wicked Haman.
five hundred men: Besides the three hundred that they slew the second day, Es 9:15.
on the spoil laid they not: By which they declared that this was God's just judgment on the enemies of his Church as they fought not for their own gain, but to execute his vengeance.
unto this day's decree: This she requires not out of a desire for vengeance but with zeal to see God's judgment's executed against his enemies.
foes seventy and five thousand: Meaning, that they laid hands on no one that was not the enemy of God.
thirteenth day of the month Adar: Meaning, in all places saving Shushan.
made the fourteenth day of the: As the Jews do even to this day, calling it in the Persian language Purim, that is, the day of lots.
these things: The Jews gather from this that Mordecai wrote this book, but it seems that he wrote only these letters and decrees that follow.
sending portions one to another: He sets before our eyes the use of this feast which was for the remembrance of God's deliverance, the maintenance of mutual friendship and relief of the poor.
Esther came before the king: That is, Esther.
device: These are the words of the kings commandment to disannul Haman's wicked enterprise.
days according to their writing: Meaning, the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar.
words of peace and truth: Which were letters declaring to them quietness and assurance and putting them out of doubt and fear.
fastings and their cry: That they would observe this feast with fasting and earnest prayer, which in Hebrew is signified by this word (they cry).
